title: Response Economics Labs — field notes & wireframe iterations
content:
Context and goal:
- Quick field notes from a whiteboard + hallway-run usability checks for a token-level cost + latency investigator panel.
- Goal: let engineers and SREs quickly answer "Which tokens or subroutines are driving cost and tail latency?" without leaving the Console.
- Audience: platform engineers, growth PMs trying to optimize per-invocation spend, SRE oncall.

High-level product hypothesis (one-liner):
If we give a compact, queryable view that atomizes an invocation into token shards (cost, CPU/GPU time, KV-cache status) plus a time-slice trace, teams will reduce median token cost by making targeted prompt or model-variant changes and will resolve tail latency incidents faster.

Quick wins to prioritize (MVP scope):
- Invocation summary row: model, route, user tag, total tokens, total cost, p50/p95 latency. Click to expand.
- Compact "token ledger": per-token rows (or grouped spans) showing token text snippet, token-index, token-cost, estimated compute-ms, cache-hit bool, and a small sparkline for latency attribution.
- Time-slice trace: horizontal timeline showing when each token was executed and where stall occurred (I/O, kernel queuing, compilation).
- Export CSV + permalink for incident annotation.

Wireframe iterations (sketch descriptions, not final UI patterns):
1) Investigator Pane (iteration A — 'dense rows'):
  - Left column: invocation meta (model selector, route, timestamp, tags).
  - Center: token ledger as dense rows, fixed-height list, allows fast scanning. Each row: [index] [token preview 8–16 chars] [cost (USD/token)] [latency-ms] [cache-icon].
  - Right column: micro-trace waterfall (stacked lanes: runtime, kernel, networking) aligned to token index via hover sync.
  - Interaction notes: hover token -> highlight corresponding range on timeline; click token -> open details drawer with full text, embeddings profile, and related requests.
  - Rationale: great for triage when you want to read a lot of invocations quickly.

2) Investigator Pane (iteration B — 'timeline-first'):
  - Full-width timeline on top. Below: token summaries grouped by time buckets (50ms slices).
  - Each time bucket shows aggregate cost, avg latency, and top contributing tokens (inline chips).
  - Rationale: better for spotting bursts and queuing behavior; trades off token-level scan speed.

3) Investigator Pane (iteration C — 'card mode / notebook'):
  - Invocation shown as a vertical scroll of cards: summary card, cost breakdown card, latency hotspots card, model-variant suggestion card.
  - Good for handoffs to non-engineers (PMs, CS) who need narrative.

Design tradeoffs we debated:
- Full token-text vs. token-preview: showing full tokens (and detokenization) is expensive and noisy, but previews can hide context. Plan: preview + expand on demand, preserve original token index mapping for reproducibility.
- Row density vs. readability: dense rows for debugging, card mode for postmortems. Provide view toggle.
- Units: display both raw ms and normalized per-GPU-ms to help correlate with cost models.
- Privacy: avoid leaking user text in shared links by default; add redact-on-share toggle.

Instrumentation & backend requirements (notes for infra/APIs):
- Need per-token cost attribution computed at serving runtime (or best-effort approximation). Ticket: PROJ-4821.
- KV-cache hit metadata must be plumbed through tracing spans for each token.
- Timeline requires synchronized timestamps from runtime (sampled at 1ms resolution recommended for initial work).
- Endpoint to fetch "compact token ledger" that supports pagination and time-slice filters.

Open questions / unresolved topics:
- How to surface quantized model differences (e.g., 4-bit vs 8-bit) in cost attribution when runtime uses heterogeneous kernels? (UX: callout badge + hover explanation)
- How many token rows to render before performance degrades? Need client-side virtualization + server-side grouping.
- Should we show token embeddings similarity to a flagged prompt-set (privacy + compute costs)?

Backlog (rough prioritization):
- P0: compact token ledger + hover-sync timeline + export CSV (owner: Eli).
- P1: canary of token-cost attribution for a single model family (owner: Priya).
- P1: redact-on-share, link permission guardrails (owner: security PM).
- P2: model-variant suggestion engine (baseline heuristics: suggest smaller quantized variant when cost > X and p95 < Y).
- P3: integrate with Rollouts to show which deploy changed token-econ over time.

Quick usability findings from 3 hallway tests (short):
- Dev A (infra): immediately looked for a p50/p95 toggle; was surprised there wasn't a way to show percentile ranges inline.
- Dev B (app PM): wanted a "most expensive span" highlight that clusters multiple adjacent tokens into one actionable unit.
- Dev C (SRE): asked for an automatic correlation to traces in App APM (server id, GPU id) – suggested a link-out.

Implementation notes for frontend engineer (practical):
- Use virtualized list (react-window or similar) for token ledger.
- Timeline should be canvas-based for performance; overlay DOM elements for interactive highlights.
- Keep a compact mobile-first fallback: stack invocation summary, then timeline, then first N token rows.

Copy / microcopy suggestions (to decrease cognitive load):
- Invocation summary header: "Invocation X — {model} • {route} • {tokens} tokens • ${cost} • p95 {latency}ms"
- Token row tooltip: "Token #{i} — cost: ${x} — compute: {y}ms — cache: {hit/miss} — origin: {prompt/system}"
- Empty state: "No token-level traces found for this invocation. Try enabling 'detailed tracing' on your route or expand the sample window."

Metrics we'll track (to validate hypothesis):
- Reduction in mean token-cost for target routes (baseline over 30d).
- Mean time-to-detect tail-latency incident after release of investigator panel.
- Feature usage: % of invocations where token-ledger was opened, average time in Investigator Pane.

Next steps / immediate actions:
- UX: convert iteration A -> low-fidelity figma (Maya) by EOD Friday.
- Eng: spike for token-cost endpoint + prototype payload size estimate (Eli, 1 week).
- Infra: add span attribute for KV-cache-hit and kernel-queue-duration (Samir, coordinate with runtime team).
- PM: create JIRA epic and link PROJ-4821 as blocker for initial rollout.

Misc notes (notes-to-self style):
- Keep language in UI neutral about pricing (avoid showing non-billable estimates without legal signoff).
- Consider an "investigator role" permission to hide raw payloads for non-admins.
- Cross-reference: CONFLUENCE:CNF-1421 has initial experiment results for a similar per-token cost idea (useful for model-variant heuristics).

Questions for review meeting:
- Do we want to include per-token model-confidence (probability) in MVP? (privacy + perf tradeoffs)
- What SLOs should the Investigator Pane have for first-load time? (suggestion: <800ms for 10-token preview, <2s for 100-token grouped view)

—— end of field notes ——
